messages.subject: Unmapped reads in the BAM file outputted from Rsubread
messages.subject_clean: Unmapped reads in the BAM file outputted from Rsubread
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

When using align function in Rsubread package to align the reads, it appears that the unmapped reads will be printed into the BAM file.

Is this true? If so, any particular reasons for this?

Is there a need to remove those unmapped reads before feeding BAM file into featureCounts in order to do the quantification analysis?

Many thanks,

Tom

messages.subject: Re: Unmapped reads in the BAM file outputted from Rsubread
messages.subject_clean: Unmapped reads in the BAM file outputted from Rsubread
messages.body_plain:
Including the unmapped reads in the BAM file is a common practice of read aligners. It preserves all the information in the fastq file input, and one can restore the fastq file from the BAM file when needed. It also helps tools that assemble the mapped and unmapped reads together to build long contigs.

I'm not sure why you hope to remove the unmapped reads from the BAM file before running featureCounts on it. Inclusion of unmapped reads will not affect the counting results.

messages.subject: Generate simplified annotation file (SAF) from multi-fasta file and/or STAR genome index
messages.subject_clean: Generate simplified annotation file (SAF) from multi-fasta file and/or STAR genome index
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I have used STAR alignment software to map RNA-seq reads to a (small) multi-fasta file after successfully generating a 'genome index' without supplying any annotation file (e.g. *.gff).

Now I would like to use featureCount of Rsubread to summarize the mapped reads for each gene contained in the multi-fasta sequence but I don't know how to best generate an annotation file (e.g. SAF) to supply to the annot.ext parameter?!

Is there a way to generate a SAF file from a multi-fasta file or use information from the STAR genome index output?

Many thanks in advance for any help and directions!

Jan

messages.body_plain:
Dear Wei,

thanks for your response.

I'm aware of the inbuilt annotations for human and mouse in Rsubread and I have also used public GTF annotation files to provide to featureCounts for counting previously.
Unfortunately, for my current analysis I don't have any GTF annotation file but only have a multi-fasta file (which I map my RNA-seq reads to).

Therefore, I currently don't know how to build my own annotation file from the available information (i.e. multi-fasta file and STAR 'genome' index) to count the reads mapped to the individual fasta sequence of my reference 'genome' using Rsubread.
Do you have any advice on that?

Many thanks in advance!

Jan

messages.subject: Re: Generate simplified annotation file (SAF) from multi-fasta file and/or STAR genome index
messages.subject_clean: Generate simplified annotation file (SAF) from multi-fasta file and/or STAR genome index
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jan,

Let's say the chr names in you fasta file is chr1, chr2, ... and their lengths are 100, 200, ...., respectively. Then you can construct the SAF annotation like below:

> GeneID Chr Start End Strand
> Chr1 Chr1 1 100 +
> Chr2 Chr2 1 200 +
> ...

You can then provide the generated SAF data frame to featureCounts for counting.
